title: Google is Having a TPU Moment
summary: Get ready to hear Google brag about TPUs on Wednesday. When Alphabet, Google’s parent company, reports third-quarter earnings tomorrow, the company’s in-house AI chips, tensor processing units, are sure to be on the lips of Google executives and Wall Street analysts. That’s because we got a bunch of new  signs this week of the swelling customer demand for TPUs.Earlier today, Googlesaidthat Oracle will become the first major cloud provider outside Google itself to begin offering TPUs to customers through its own data centers. And a short while ago, Ryan Barwickpublished a scoopfor us that says OpenAI—a major customer for Nvidia’s AI chips—plans to buy Google’s TPUs.But perhaps the juiciest details on TPU demand came on Monday courtesy of Anthropic’s IPO prospectus. In that filing, Anthropic chronicled the enormity of the financial commitment it has made to the Google chips, including a plan to spend $114.5 billion with Google Cloud (it didn’t specify how much of that will be for TPU-based compute). Anthropic also estimated it could spend an additional $125 billion to $150 billion on TPUs with Google and other providers. And the AI company will pony up $161.2 billion for TPU compute with Broadcom, which co-designs TPUs with Google.TPUs, you’ll recall, began as chips that Google used only internally starting over a decade ago. The company began allowing outside customers to use them via Google Cloud in 2018. More recently, Google has begun striking agreements with companies like Fluidstack and now Oracle to run TPUs in their own data centers. Google only began recognizing revenue from the sale of TPUs to outside data centers last quarter, though Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi said on an earnings call then that only a small portion of the revenues from its TPU agreements were reflected during that period. The “vast majority of revenues” from those agreements will kick in next year, Ashkenazi said.Analysts are predicting something of a windfall for Google when th
title_es: El momento de los TPU: Google consolida demanda empresarial de chips
bajada: Google está experimentando un crecimiento acelerado en demanda de sus TPUs. La evidencia incluye Oracle como primer proveedor cloud en ofrecer TPUs, OpenAI como nuevo cliente, y Anthropic comprometiéndose a gastar entre $114.5B y $400B en TPU compute.
bajada_en: Google is experiencing accelerated demand growth for its TPUs. Evidence includes Oracle becoming the first cloud provider outside Google to offer TPUs, OpenAI as a new customer, and Anthropic committing $114.5B-$400B in TPU compute spending.

title: OpenAI, a Longtime Nvidia Customer, Plans to Buy Google’s AI Chips
summary: OpenAIplans to buyGoogle’s AI chips, according to a person familiar with the matter, in a boost for a rising competitor to OpenAI backer Nvidia.Financial terms and other details of OpenAI’s planned purchase couldn’t be learned. But any deal for it to buy tensor processing units would be a big win for Google’s chip business, which is a growingchallengerto the Nvidia graphics processing units that have dominated the market for AI computing power. OpenAI has been one of the most valuable customers for Nvidia, which in turn has invested tens of billions of dollars in the startup.
title_es: OpenAI planea comprar chips de IA de Google desafiando el dominio de Nvidia
bajada: OpenAI, uno de los mayores clientes de Nvidia, planea adquirir unidades de procesamiento tensorial (TPUs) de Google. El movimiento representa un cambio significativo en la estrategia de chips de IA y fortalece a Google como competidor en el mercado de computación para IA.
bajada_en: OpenAI, one of Nvidia's largest customers, plans to acquire Google's tensor processing units (TPUs). The move signals a significant shift in AI chip strategy and strengthens Google as a competitor in the AI computing market.

title: Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication

bajada_en: A family sues OpenAI alleging ChatGPT convinced their daughter to stop seizure medication, resulting in her death in February. The case raises critical concerns about AI liability in medical advice.

bajada_en: Anthropic acquired Mithril Medicine, a startup focused on developing treatments for muscular dystrophy. The acquisition is part of the company's strategy to expand its capabilities in AI-applied drug discovery.

bajada_en: NVIDIA released a free speech-to-text model supporting transcription in 40 languages, though it only works on recordings, not live audio. The advance is significant for meeting and medical transcription tools, while ElevenLabs retains the edge on live audio.

title: ‘Nobody’s Ready’: AI-Found Bugs Spark a Corporate Security Spending Spree
summary: A week ago, Vijay Rayapati, CEO of enterprise software startup Atomicwork, gathered his team of roughly 30 software engineers and told them to drop everything and prioritize cybersecurity.A series of cybersecurity incidents over the prior 48 hours demanded the company’s immediate attention: eMudhra, a so-called root certificate authority, which websites and software makers rely on to prove their identity to users, had been hacked; LiteLLM, a popular open-source tool for routing requests to different AI models, was compromised; and a security vulnerability had been found in PHP, a programming language used by roughly 70% of websites.While the startup ultimately verified that it wasn’t directly impacted by the threats, the fact that it was scrambling last week “shows nobody’s ready,” Rayapati said. He is planning to hire one cybersecurity engineer for every three technical hires his company makes, and projects the number of cybersecurity-focused engineers will roughly triple to 27 in the year ahead.
title_es: Bugs encontrados por IA disparan gastos en ciberseguridad corporativa
bajada: Una serie de vulnerabilidades de seguridad críticas (eMudhra, LiteLLM, PHP) demostró que las empresas no están preparadas para responder a incidentes de IA. Esto está generando una ola de contrataciones en ciberseguridad, con empresas como Atomicwork triplicando su equipo de seguridad.
bajada_en: A series of critical security vulnerabilities (eMudhra, LiteLLM, PHP) revealed that enterprises are unprepared to respond to AI-driven incidents. This is sparking a wave of cybersecurity hiring, with companies like Atomicwork tripling their security teams.
